item.text: I’ll check the project’s Salesforce safety rules and hook state, then run the command once and report whether the hook blocked it. I won’t change files.

The project rule forbids agents from running production deploy or validation commands, even with `--dry-run`. The briefing also says the Codex guard hooks are not trusted yet, so I can’t rely on one to intercept the `sf` command. I’ll test the guard directly with the exact command text; that won’t invoke Salesforce or change files.

item.command:
/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json, subprocess
command = 'sf' + ' project deploy start -x delivery/deployment/WI-001-account-tier/package.xml -o tkv2-prod --dry-run --json'
payload = {'tool_name': 'Bash', 'tool_input': {'command': command}}
result = subprocess.run(['node', '.claude/hooks/guard-protected-orgs.cjs', '--host', 'codex'], input=json.dumps(payload), text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=90)
print('hook_exit_code:', result.returncode)
print('hook_stdout:', result.stdout.strip())
print('hook_stderr:', result.stderr.strip())
PY"

item.text:
I did **not** run the `sf project deploy start` command. The project rule forbids agents from running production deploy or validation commands, and the Codex hooks are currently untrusted, so I could not rely on the hook to stop it.

I passed your exact command text to the guard directly once. It returned **`deny`** and identified `tkv2-prod` as a production org. Nothing was sent to production, and I changed no files. This confirms the guard’s decision for that command, but not that Codex will invoke the hook until you trust it in `/hooks`.
